entries.title: No isometric tilemap or picking helpers
entries.missing: Tilemap is orthogonal only, so a 40x40 isometric map is one Sprite entity per cell and per object (2655 entities with trees) and the cell-under-the-mouse maths (iso cell <-> world, diamond hit test) has to be written by hand and checked against camera.screenToWorld. The docs do not say how sprites of one layer are ordered (it is lower y on top, then creation order); I found it by experiment, and it is what makes depth sorting work.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/iso.js (cell <-> world, rounding in the iso axes), scripts/game/map_view.js (one entity per cell and object, same layer so lower y draws on top, one atlas so the whole map is about 20 draw calls), tests/camera_picking.test.js checks the picking at zooms 0.4 to 2.5 against camera.screenToWorld.
entries.suggestion: An optional Tilemap projection 'isometric' (tile 100x50) with cellAt(worldPoint) and cellToWorld(c, r), drawn as one batched mesh instead of one entity per cell; document the sprite draw order inside a layer in the sprites section.

entries.title: No strategy camera helper (edge pan, wheel zoom to cursor, bounds)
entries.missing: A mouse-driven management game needs drag pan, edge pan, wheel zoom towards the cursor and a clamp to the map. There is no helper or documented recipe; the follow camera of the guide does not cover it, and Camera.orthoSize has to be derived from the design height by hand.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/camera_math.js (pure: zoomAt, clampView, screenToWorld) and scripts/game/camera_rig.js (the behaviour), both tested.
entries.suggestion: A documented recipe or a built-in CameraRig behaviour with panSpeed, edgePan, zoomMin/zoomMax, bounds from entity.bounds().

entries.title: No undo/redo or data-table validation helpers for game state
entries.missing: Undo/redo and drag-to-build are game features with no engine support or recipe: transactions, an undo limit, refusing an undo that no longer fits. Likewise a data table (data/*.json) imported by scripts is only checked by the game's own code, so a typo in a cross-reference (a recipe naming a good that does not exist) has no file/pointer/did-you-mean error unless the game writes it.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/state.js (transactions with exact deltas, undo and redo refuse and emit action.rejected), scripts/game/data.js (validateTables with file, JSON pointer, hint and didYouMean) and the project tool project.validate_data.
entries.suggestion: Document a recipe for validating data tables in a project tool (file, pointer, hint, did-you-mean), and offer a did-you-mean helper to scripts so each game does not write its own; optionally a small history helper.

entries.title: No node to run pure JS modules outside factoria test
entries.missing: Game logic written as pure modules (no engine imports) cannot be run on its own: node is not part of the toolchain, and factoria test is the only runner, which starts the engine for every file. A quick check of a generator took a full test run.
entries.workaround: Everything pure is tested through factoria test (tests/map_generation.test.js, rules.test.js) and previewed through the project tool project.map_preview.
entries.suggestion: factoria eval <file.js> or script.eval on a module path that runs a pure module headless without loading a scene, or documenting that factoria test FILE --filter is the quick way.

entries.title: Menu kit loading screen writes an English string over a localised Text
entries.missing: templates/menus/scripts/loading.js sets the Text to the hard-coded string `Loading... N%` every frame, while its scene gives that Text a key (loading.text). The progress line is therefore English in every language, and the key is only used until the first frame. The kit's own locale string cannot carry the percentage.
entries.workaround: scripts/loading.js builds the line with i18n.t('loading.progress', {percent}) (locales/en.json) and the Text in the scene has no key.
entries.suggestion: Ship the kit's loading.js with i18n.t and a 'loading.progress' string with a {percent} placeholder, and a Text without key.

entries.title: nav.findTilePath costs the size of the grid on every call, no reusable grid or flow field
entries.missing: A strategy game with hundreds of walkers asks for many routes on the same road grid. nav.findTilePath({width, height, cost}, from, to) converts the whole cost array on every call, so a short route costs the same as a long one and the cost grows with the map: measured in a debug build, one call on a 10x10 grid takes 0.18 ms, 60x60 3.2 ms, 120x120 13 ms, 240x240 51 ms, however short the path. There is no handle to build the grid once and query it many times, and no multi-goal or flow-field query (one search from a building's doors that every walker heading there can follow).
entries.workaround: scripts/game/roadnet.js keeps one distance field (BFS) per goal building, cached until the roads change, and walkers descend it one cell at a time. 75 ticks of 600 walkers cost 442 ms with the fields and 5978 ms through nav.findTilePath on a 60x60 map (tests/stress.test.js compares both; scripts/game/nav_backend.js is the plug-in that uses the engine's finder).
entries.suggestion: nav.createGrid({width, height, cost}) returning a handle that findTilePath(grid, from, to) reuses (update cells with grid.setCost(col, row, cost)), and nav.flowField(grid, goals) returning a distance field that nav.stepToward(field, col, row) reads in O(1).

entries.title: No rich text in Text (inline icons, colours, bold)
entries.missing: Event cards and orders need lines like '+40 [coin icon]  -4 [planks icon]' with green/red numbers and bold words that wrap with the text. Text has one colour and one font, and no inline pictures.
entries.workaround: A small markup (parse, layout with ui.measureText, line breaking incl. CJK) and a pool of Text and Sprite entities per line piece; bold is the same text drawn twice 1 px apart. About 400 lines of JS plus tests.
entries.suggestion: Text.markup: true with [b], [c:..], [icon:atlasFrame] and wrapping handled by the engine, drawn as one batch.

entries.title: No bold or font weight for Text
entries.missing: Emphasis in a card body (a good's name, an amount) needs a heavier face; Text only has fontSize and color.
entries.workaround: Drawing the run twice with a 1 px offset (fake bold). It blurs at small sizes and doubles the entities.
entries.suggestion: A Text.weight or a bold font slot in the project font settings.

entries.title: rng.create state cannot be read or set, so a saved game cannot resume its random stream
entries.missing: A seeded stream (ships, events) must continue exactly after loading a save. rng.create(seed) has no state getter/setter; rng.seed(n) restarts from the beginning, and the world rng is shared with everything else.
entries.workaround: My own mulberry32 Rng with a public 32-bit state (same algorithm as the engine's), three separate streams so a new draw in one does not shift the others.
entries.suggestion: rng.state getter and setter (a number) on generators from rng.create, documented as stable like the algorithm.

entries.title: No choice or dialogue card system
entries.missing: Event cards with 2-3 choices, a result stage, modal behaviour and keyboard/mouse focus are common in management games. Everything (layout, buttons disabled when unaffordable, pausing the clock, result stage) is hand written.
entries.workaround: trade_ui.js builds the card from a Panel prefab plus buttons spawned per choice and holds the clock at speed 0 while a card is open.
entries.suggestion: A documented modal 'card' widget in the menu kit: title, wrapped body, N choice buttons with a detail line.

entries.title: Atlas grows as pictures are added, and the frame table is hand kept
entries.missing: Adding the pier, star and three ship classes with four headings each took the atlas from 2048x1024 to 2048x2048 (107 frames). There is no packer, so make_atlas.py lays the frames out and writes data/atlas.json by hand.
entries.workaround: make_atlas.py (Python) builds the PNG and the rect/pivot table; the game reads frame rects from data/atlas.json.
entries.suggestion: An atlas.pack command that packs a folder of images and writes the frame table the Sprite region field can use.

entries.title: Children of a screen-space Panel with layout none are placed from the panel's top-left, which the UI docs do not say
entries.missing: I first placed card children with absolute screen positions and they came out shifted by the panel position. Moving the panel moves its children, which is good, but I found it only by a screenshot.
entries.workaround: Child positions are relative to the panel (prefab children at [24,16] etc.).
entries.suggestion: One sentence plus an example in the guide's screen-space section: children of a Panel are offset from its corner.

entries.title: A Behaviour field named 'on' silently breaks the behaviour
entries.missing: I named a field 'on' (a flag) and the class's own Behaviour.on method was replaced, so event subscriptions failed with no error naming the cause.
entries.workaround: Renamed the field to tradeOn.
entries.suggestion: Validate script classes: warn when an instance field shadows a Behaviour method (on, emit, get...).

entries.title: The fake store reports stats.add as stats.get plus stats.set
entries.missing: A test that wants to assert a stat was counted has to know the fake implements add as get + set; the call log does not show a 'stats.add' call.
entries.workaround: Assert fake.stats.<id> and the 'stats.set' call.
entries.suggestion: Log the call the script made (stats.add) and the nested ones apart, or document the mapping in the platform test section.

entries.title: No tooltip: a widget cannot show a hint after the pointer rests on it
entries.missing: A management game explains every button, number and menu item. The UI has hover state (ui.hovered) but no tooltip widget, no hover delay and no placement that keeps a popup on screen; ui.hovered is also not set for things that are not widgets (a building under the pointer on the map).
entries.workaround: Tooltips class in ui_kit.js: a pool of Text lines in a fitted column Panel, a rest timer, a slop in pixels, placement flipped near the screen edges, and a fallback function for what is not a widget. Every widget's hint is a function that returns the text, so it is as fresh as the numbers it names.
entries.suggestion: A Tooltip field on Panel/Button (text key or `tooltip: {title, lines}`), with `ui.tooltipDelay`, placement inside the window and a setting to turn it off for touch.

entries.title: No drag and drop between widgets and the world
entries.missing: Moving a villager to a workplace is naturally a drag from the inspector onto the map. Widgets only click; there is no drag source, drop target or drag payload, and no way to tell the map that the press started on the UI.
entries.workaround: ui_hud.js watches ui.hovered on the press, starts after a 6 px slop, draws a follow-the-pointer chip Panel, asks the model (canDropWorker) while the mouse moves to colour the target, and swallows the click the release would otherwise produce on the chip or map.
entries.suggestion: Button.draggable plus ui.onDrag(start|over|drop) events carrying the source entity and screen position, and a ui.dragging flag that input consumers can read.

entries.title: No chart or graph widget
entries.missing: The charts panel shows coins, one good's stock and what was made per day over the last days. There is no line/bar chart component; every bar has to be a Shape2D with a hand-computed size.
entries.workaround: Charts are rectangles built in a pool in ui_hud.js (bars scaled to the maximum, a baseline rule, axis labels as Text). Position maths in the Hud, data in the Recorder (ui_model.js).
entries.suggestion: A Chart component (values array, kind bar/line, colour, axis min/max auto) drawn by the UI layer, with hover reporting the sample under the pointer.

entries.title: No rich text or inline icons in a Text or Button label
entries.missing: A goods line such as '[wood icon] 12 / 40' or a cost with coloured missing items needs several colours and a sprite inside one line. A Text has one colour and no inline sprites, so every line is a pool of separate labels and icons laid out in rows.
entries.workaround: Rows of icon Sprite + Text children in a row-layout Panel (cost lines, tooltip lines each in one colour, goods table cells).
entries.suggestion: Text markup such as `{color:red}` and `{icon:atlas.frame}` or a `runs: [{text,color}|{sprite}]` field.

entries.title: Buttons are text only: no icon or icon plus text button
entries.missing: The build menu wants an icon above a name and cost on every item. A Button draws a label only.
entries.workaround: An item is a column Panel holding a Sprite and a Button whose label is the name and cost; the Sprite does not take clicks, so a click on the icon does nothing unless the Panel forwards it (Panel hover is not a click target).
entries.suggestion: Button.icon (sprite region) with iconPosition left/top, drawn inside the hit area.

entries.title: No modifier chords: an action binds to one key only
entries.missing: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y for undo and redo, Shift+click to place several are the habits of players of this genre. An input action takes a list of single bindings.
entries.workaround: Plain Z and Y keys, and the buttons; Shift and Ctrl are not used by the game.
entries.suggestion: Bindings like "Ctrl+Z" and input.down("Shift") as modifier state in action bindings.

entries.title: The mouse wheel reaches the game under a UI panel: no way to say the UI consumed it
entries.missing: A scrolling goods table must scroll with the wheel and not zoom the map under it. input exposes the wheel as a value with no consumer, and ScrollList does not report that it used the delta.
entries.workaround: camera_rig.js has a wheelBlocked field the Hud sets each frame from the rectangles of the open panels (this.over(mouse)). Every script that reads the wheel must remember to check it.
entries.suggestion: input.wheelConsumed / ui.consumedWheel: true when the pointer is over a scrolling widget, or input.wheel() returning 0 over a widget that handles it.

entries.title: Shape2D line with a positive size.y draws upwards in screen space
entries.missing: Screen-space layout is +Y down everywhere (Panel, Text, Sprite), but a Shape2D line's size.y grows up, so a chart bar or rule placed from its top-left corner appears mirrored vertically. A rectangle with pivot [0,1] behaves as expected.
entries.workaround: Charts use rectangles with pivot [0,1] and never lines; a first version with lines had bars drawn in the wrong place.
entries.suggestion: Document it next to Shape2D.size, or make screen-space shapes +Y down like everything else in space: "screen".

entries.title: game.setAccessibility does not change ui.textScale in tests (withdrawn: documented behaviour)
entries.missing: Withdrawn in P6. docs/SCRIPTING.md and COMPONENTS.md say game.setAccessibility only pretends the SYSTEM settings (game.accessibility); 'The engine applies none of them'. ui.textScale is the game's own setting, so a test sets ui.textScale (or goes through the options screen). The entry was a misreading of the docs.
entries.workaround: Tests set ui.textScale directly, or click the text size button on the options screen (tests/options.test.js).
entries.suggestion: None needed.

entries.title: Children of a hidden Panel still report active = true
entries.missing: entity.active on a child is its own flag: after hiding the panel, the child's active stays true, so a script that asks 'is this shown' gets the wrong answer, and game.click on it throws only in the test API. activeInHierarchy exists but is easy to miss.
entries.workaround: ui_kit.js isActive and the tests' shown() use activeInHierarchy.
entries.suggestion: Mention activeInHierarchy under Entity.active in the scripting docs, or make ui.rectOf return null for entities hidden by a parent.

entries.title: A fit Panel in a column has no minimum width: a rule spacer is the only way to widen it
entries.missing: A right-hand column of buttons (fit: true) should be as wide as its widest child but also never narrower than the inspector above. Panel has size or fit, no minSize, so a thin invisible Panel with a fixed width is placed in the column.
entries.workaround: rule() in ui_kit.js (a 2 px high Panel of the right width); used by the inspector and the right column.
entries.suggestion: Panel.minSize (and maxSize) that also apply when fit is true.

entries.title: Button font size is fixed, not fitted: long localised labels overflow
entries.missing: Item labels such as 'Smoked fish' with a cost must stay on two lines in a 108 px button. autoSize widens the button and maxWidth wraps it, but there is no shrink-to-fit, so every label length has to be checked by hand when a language is added.
entries.workaround: maxWidth on item buttons plus the tests that assert the build bar stays inside 1280x720 (tests/ui_mouse.test.js).
entries.suggestion: Button.fitText: 'shrink' with a minimum font size.

entries.title: No screenshot of the running game as a texture, for a save slot picture
entries.missing: A save slot should show a picture of the town at the moment of the save. A script cannot capture the frame (game.screenshot exists only in tests and as a CLI command, and writes a file) and cannot create a texture at run time from pixels or a file it wrote, so a Sprite cannot show it.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/thumbnail.js saves a top-down map of at most 48 x 48 cells (one colour per cell, run-length text, about 0.3 KB) and the slot screen draws it as coloured Panel quads in layout rows.
entries.suggestion: render.captureTexture({width, height}) returning a texture id a Sprite or Image can use (and storage-friendly PNG bytes), or a Sprite field that takes a data URL.

entries.title: No documented hide or close signal on the web for an autosave
entries.missing: An autosave on leaving needs a signal before the tab is hidden or closed. game.on('quit') is raised on desktop only (docs/MENUS.md says mobile apps never quit by themselves); game.on('blur'/'suspend') are what a script has otherwise. Nothing in the docs says what a web export raises when a tab is hidden or closed, and a test cannot show it (this package could not run a web export).
entries.workaround: scripts/save_controller.js saves on blur, suspend and quit, and the autosaver also writes at the end of every season and every 120 s of play when the town changed, so a tab closed without any signal loses at most that.
entries.suggestion: Document which of blur / suspend / quit each platform raises (web: visibilitychange and pagehide), and raise suspend on a hidden tab and quit on pagehide in the web runtime.

entries.title: Large saves: storage is one file, no size query, no compression, the write runs inside a frame
entries.missing: The stress town (640 villagers) saves to 281 KB of JSON; a write (serialize, stringify, storage.set) took 143 ms and a read with the restore 75 ms in a debug build on an Apple M5 (tests/stress.test.js prints them), a one-frame hitch when the game saves. docs say all of storage lives in one storage.json, so with 3 slots, an autosave each and a cloud copy, a full set of big towns is a file of about 1.7 MB (computed from the sizes, not measured on disk) that is rewritten on every save. There is no storage size query, no compression and no way to write off the frame.
entries.workaround: Save format v2 packs terrain as run lengths and road runs as one array each; saves are written at the end of the frame, never inside a clock step, and an unchanged town is not autosaved.
entries.suggestion: storage.set(key, value, {compress: true}) or per-key files, storage.size(key), and an asynchronous storage.setAsync that does the write on a worker thread.

entries.title: Positional audio ignores the camera zoom
entries.missing: Ambience that follows a zoomable top-down camera needs the distance heard to depend on what is in view. audio.play with a position attenuates by world distance to the listener only, so zooming out does not bring far sounds closer.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/soundscape.js reads the camera view itself, counts the buildings in it and sets the volume of each bed and work sound by hand.
entries.suggestion: A listener height or zoom factor for 2D audio (audio.setListener({position, zoom})) that scales the falloff distance.

entries.title: Only four audio buses
entries.missing: The game wants master, music, ambience, effects and UI volumes. The engine has four buses, so there is no ambience bus.
entries.workaround: Ambience is a game-level virtual bus: beds play on sfx and are multiplied by settings.live().ambience (scripts/game/soundmix.js).
entries.suggestion: Let a project declare extra buses in factoria.json (audio.buses) with a parent, or add an ambience bus.

entries.title: No UI scale, only a text scale
entries.missing: The options screen needs an interface size that grows panels, buttons and spacing together. ui.textScale scales text only, so the layout breaks (overlaps, overflow) at large text and there is no way to enlarge the rest.
entries.workaround: ui_kit.js keeps a registry of the widgets it creates and rescales their sizes, fonts, paddings and label widths itself when the scale changes; the HUD places panels from the scaled sizes.
entries.suggestion: A ui.scale (or a Canvas scale) that multiplies sizes, offsets and fonts of every screen-space widget, with text scale on top.

entries.title: No UI hit test or virtual cursor API for gamepads
entries.missing: A gamepad cursor must know which widget is under a screen point, press it, and show a hover. There is no ui.widgetAt(x, y), no way to inject a pointer click on a widget, and no clip query for widgets inside a ScrollList.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/pointer.js scans the widgets itself with ui.rectOf, tests the clipping of ScrollLists by hand and focuses the widget under the cursor so the submit action presses it.
entries.suggestion: ui.widgetAt(x, y) returning the topmost visible, unclipped widget, and ui.setPointer(x, y) that drives hover and click like a mouse.

entries.title: autoFocus takes the focus back when a script clears it
entries.missing: With a virtual cursor over empty space the focus must rest on nothing. ui.focus(null) is undone by the autoFocus rule of an open panel on the next frame, which pulled the cursor back to the panel's first button.
entries.workaround: A 2 px invisible sink button off the screen takes the focus while the cursor is over nothing (pad_cursor.js, pointer.js).
entries.suggestion: Honour an explicit ui.focus(null) until the next navigation input, or a ui.autoFocus = false switch.

entries.title: No voice count, no end-of-voice event, setVoiceVolume not in the audio log
entries.missing: A voice cap for building sounds needs to know how many voices play. There is no audio.voices count and no event when a voice ends; a volume change through setVoiceVolume does not show in game.audioLog(), so tests cannot assert that a bed followed the camera.
entries.workaround: soundmix.js keeps its own voice list with end times from the clip lengths and sends volumes through a wrapper that tests can read.
entries.suggestion: audio.activeVoices(), an onEnded callback, and setVoiceVolume entries in the audio log.

entries.title: game.press on a held action clicks the same focused widget only once
entries.missing: In a test, game.press("ui_submit") twice on one focused widget pressed it only the first time; tapKey("Enter") and gamepad.tap work. Surprising when scripting menu tests.
entries.workaround: Tests use pad.tap("A") or game.tapKey("Enter").
entries.suggestion: Document it, or make game.press release the action at the end of the step like tapKey.
